t: Handle pharmacy refill calls with a voice agent
s: A pharmacy's phone agent identifies callers, submits refills, and routes renewal requests to prescribers.
did: The pharmacy put a voice agent on its refill line. It confirms who is calling, checks the prescription, submits the refill, or queues a renewal request for the prescriber.
how: It handled about 380 refills in its first 30 days. Calls it can't resolve go to staff.

t: Book property viewings and follow up with leads
s: An n8n sales assistant books site visits, sends follow-up emails, and updates the CRM for a real-estate team.
did: The builder connected n8n to email, a calendar and the CRM. The agent answers lead questions, offers viewing times, books them, and logs each step.
how: It runs daily with no manual booking. The poster didn't share conversion numbers.

t: Reconcile supplier invoices and invoice clients automatically
s: A business owner's agent matches supplier invoices, reports pricing and freight, and invoices clients through Zoho Books.
did: The owner built a small CRM with an agent behind it. It reads supplier invoices, matches them to orders, places supplier orders, and raises client invoices through the Zoho Books API.
how: Reconciliation that took hours now runs on its own, with a pricing and freight report as a bonus.

t: Triage dealership customer texts by sentiment
s: A car dealership group's Make flow reads customer texts, closes routine ones, and flags unhappy customers.
did: Every inbound text runs through a sentiment check. Routine messages get closed with a reply; negative ones go straight to the aftersales team.
how: It auto-closed about 18,000 of 47,000 messages, so staff only saw the ones that needed a person.

t: Screen job candidates and handle outreach
s: A Make scenario parses resumes, scores candidates, updates the ATS, and sends shortlists to recruiters in Slack.
did: Resumes land in a folder. The flow extracts each one, scores it against the role, writes the result to the ATS, emails an acknowledgment, and posts a shortlist to Slack.
how: Published as a vendor how-to, so no real-world results are reported.

t: Mark student reports and build an assessment dashboard
s: A primary teacher had Claude build an app that marks reports, plus a dashboard for assessment data.
did: The teacher described the marking rubric and the data they track. Claude built a marking app, a dashboard, and a skill that lines up lesson ideas with the curriculum.
how: Marking time dropped, and the dashboard replaced a manual spreadsheet.

t: Split scanned homework and log it per student
s: A Claude Code skill reads names on batch scans, splits the PDF per student, and updates the completion sheet.
did: Teachers scan a stack of handwritten homework in one go. The skill reads each name, matches it to the class roster, splits the PDF, and marks the tracker.
how: Missing work gets flagged automatically, which used to take a manual pass every week.

t: Redline a contract as Word tracked changes
s: A lawyer had Claude rewrite two sections of a 30-page document and reply to comments as tracked changes.
did: Working inside Word, the lawyer asked Claude to revise two sections and answer the reviewer comments, keeping every edit as a native tracked change.
how: The lawyer judged the result better than Microsoft's built-in assistant and kept full control of what to accept.

t: Cut a hospital bill using Medicare price analysis
s: Claude priced every billing code on a $195,628 hospital bill against Medicare rates; the patient then negotiated.
did: The patient shared the itemized bill. Claude built a spreadsheet of Medicare prices for each code, showing where charges ran far above them.
how: Using that analysis, the patient negotiated about $163,000 off. The patient wrote the letters; Claude only analyzed.

t: Calculate US taxes from 1099s and brokerage statements
s: ChatGPT computed a full US tax picture from 1099s, a self-employment spreadsheet, and brokerage statements.
did: The poster uploaded their 1099 forms, a spreadsheet of self-employed income and expenses, and brokerage statements, then asked for the full calculation.
how: The numbers matched a professional's result in their case study.

t: Run Meta ad campaigns for a newsletter
s: A Claude Code agent made ad images, ran Meta campaigns through the API, and built landing-page variants.
did: The agent generated creative, launched and adjusted campaigns via the Meta API, built landing page variants, and pulled analytics each day.
how: About 50 variants were tested over 31 days. The write-up shares the process more than the final cost per subscriber.

t: Find technical SEO problems and generate the fixes
s: An SEO agent crawled a site, found broken canonicals and orphaned pages, ranked them, and wrote code fixes.
did: The author tested five SEO agents. The best one browsed the whole site, listed issues by likely impact, and produced the code changes for each.
how: It found broken canonical tags, orphaned pages, and missing schema; two other agents only pulled Search Console data.

t: Reorder low stock from suppliers automatically
s: Each morning a system checks Shopify inventory and emails a ready-made order to the right supplier.
did: The store owner set reorder levels per product. A daily job compares stock against them and emails the matching supplier a pre-written order.
how: Stockouts stopped, and the owner no longer checks inventory by hand.

t: Answer support tickets from Freshdesk history
s: A SaaS owner connected ChatGPT to Freshdesk and internal tools, then pulled back from full autonomy.
did: The agent could read past tickets and use internal tools to draft and send answers.
how: Picking the right answer, and knowing when not to answer, proved unreliable. It now drafts and a person sends.

t: Handle store customer support with an AI agent
s: A merchant ran Gorgias's AI agent for months, then switched it off.
did: The agent answered customer emails and chats for an online store.
how: It gave irrelevant answers and promised things the store couldn't deliver, so the merchant disabled it.

t: Run a contractor's back-office paperwork
s: A contractor's agent flagged an insurance certificate mismatch, created work orders, and filled a credit application.
did: The agent read contracts and certificates in the contractor's files and email, then produced work orders and forms.
how: It caught an insurance discrepancy before a job started, which the contractor said would have been missed.

t: Turn orders into Xero purchase orders, invoices and bills
s: A Make setup creates Xero purchase orders from monday.com, emails client invoices, and matches supplier bills.
did: When an order changes status in monday.com, the flow creates the Xero PO, sends the client invoice, and matches uploaded supplier invoices to bills.
how: Anything that fails to match is flagged for a person instead of guessed.

t: Automate a bookkeeping firm's routine workflows
s: A bookkeeping firm used n8n to automate recurring client work.
did: Repetitive steps such as collecting statements, chasing documents and preparing entries became n8n workflows.
how: The firm estimates about 600 hours saved a year.

t: Turn bug reports into fix pull requests
s: Sentry's analysis hands the root cause to a Cursor cloud agent, which writes the fix and opens a PR.
did: When Sentry finds the root cause of an error, it passes the context to Cursor's agent. The agent writes a fix and opens a pull request in the repo.
how: Developers review and merge the PR, so nothing ships without a person.

t: Move a company website off its CMS
s: Cursor agents moved a company site from a CMS to code and Markdown in three days.
did: The engineer had agents convert content and refactor the site, with sub-agents splitting the broad changes.
how: It took three days and about $260 in model costs.

t: Watch for and book a hard-to-get restaurant table
s: A travel agent watched a popular restaurant for an opening, booked a table for two, and texted confirmation.
did: The user named the restaurant and party size. The agent checked for openings until one appeared, then booked it.
how: It secured an 8:45pm table and sent a text confirmation.

t: Screen new founders for venture investing
s: An investor's agents watch new company filings, research founders, and draft outreach to promising matches.
did: The system monitors new filings, researches each founder, flags ones that match the fund's thesis, then drafts outreach and preps meeting questions.
how: Outreach and scheduling run without the investor doing first-pass research.

t: Handle product questions, warranties and returns by voice
s: A consumer electronics brand rebuilt its global phone support on voice agents in several languages.
did: Voice agents answer product questions, process warranty claims and start returns, in multiple languages.
how: Reported in a vendor case study; figures are the vendor's own.

t: Handle follow-ups after every meeting
s: An agent finds the transcript, pulls out action items, messages teammates, and books the next meeting.
did: After a meeting ends, the agent reads the transcript, lists action items, posts them to Slack, and checks calendars to schedule a follow-up.
how: Shown as a vendor demo, so no real-world results are reported.

t: Coordinate a family member's medical records and care
s: A family gave a relative's records to an agent, which caught a medication schedule error and a transcription mistake.
did: The family used the agent as a coordinator across doctors, records and test results.
how: It flagged a wrong pain-medication schedule and an error in genetic test markers, which changed the treatment plan.

t: Collect grant listings from many countries
s: A Zapier agent searches the web for grants in different countries and adds them to Airtable.
did: The agent runs searches by country and program type, then writes each grant it finds as a row in Airtable.
how: It works, but the user is still tuning which results to keep.

t: Draft an evidence-backed insurance appeal
s: ChatGPT helped build an employment insurance appeal that was accepted, and a home flooding appeal.
did: The user gave ChatGPT the denial letter, policy terms and evidence, then built the appeal argument point by point.
how: The employment insurance appeal was accepted.

t: Find and parse chemical safety data sheets
s: An app built with Manus finds the right SDS PDF online, downloads it, and turns it into structured data.
did: Given a product name, the system searches for the safety data sheet, downloads the PDF, extracts the text and maps it to a fixed schema.
how: The author built almost the whole app through Manus.
